Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

Score Step 2 of the SFCC-236 build (ZimmSizeChip atom + ZimmSizeChipGroup molecule) against the six axes. Round 1, no prior rework.

Files: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSizeChip.css.ts}, overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts}, + 2-import/2-entry diff in overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts.

## Orchestrator verdict: IN SCOPE
All 8 files exactly per manifest, Tier 2 diff exactly 2 imports + 2 entries (running total 3 of Marcel's pre-approved 6). Every pass criterion evidenced with file:line. Zero "SizeSelector"/zimmDropdown/useZimmSizeSelector residue. zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatchGroup untouched. No package.json change. The self-flagged `isFocusable` prop deviation verified as genuine precedent reuse from `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:38` (identical name/type/mechanism), not scope creep. No Tier 1 touch.

## Tester findings (two required mutation-and-revert falsifications performed, both confirmed working; Tester went further and found two more defects via additional unprompted mutation testing)

1. **🟡 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — `zimmSizeChip.css.ts:15,21`: `resolveBorderColour`/`resolveBackgroundColour` both use `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` (a `text.*` token) on `borderColor`/`background` properties for the Selected state. Correct-category tokens already exist at the identical value: `--zimm-color-border-focus` (already used by `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`'s own selected-border) and `--zimm-color-bg-05`/`--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-default`. Zero-visual-diff, drop-in fix. UNIFORM because the same category error already exists in `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `primary` variant (not introduced here, copied from an existing pattern) — this is now the SECOND time this exact shape has appeared in this build (first was Step 1's `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts`, already fixed in that step's round 2).

2. **🟡 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — i18n extraction never run. `size_chips.group.label` (defined via `defineMessages`) is absent from `translations/{default,en-US,en-GB}.json`, unlike `colour_swatches.*` which IS present (fixed by a prior real commit `50acf25`). Tester verified by actually running `npm run extract-default-translations`, watching it add the missing key, then reverting the Tier-2-owned translation files. Runtime falls back to English gracefully, but non-English storefronts get an English-only accessible name until this runs. UNIFORM: the same gap recurred for Step 1's `slide_indicator.position.label` too — this is the second occurrence in this build, not a one-off.

3. **🔴 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF but pattern is UNIFORM-worthy** — `zimmSizeChipGroup/index.test.tsx:91-99` ("falls back to the first ENABLED size when the first size is disabled") is a genuine tautology. Tester mutated `firstEnabledIndex` to unconditionally `return 0` (simulating a real regression: roving-tabindex fallback landing on a DISABLED chip) and the test PASSED anyway — because it asserts via `toHaveTextContent('S')`, and `'XS'.includes('S') === true`, so the disabled "XS" chip's label satisfies the assertion meant to catch exactly this bug. A sibling test with no label-substring overlap correctly failed under the same mutation, proving the vulnerability is specific to this one assertion's label choice, not a framework-wide issue. Tester's fix recommendation: assert on `data-size-value="s"` or use exact-name `getByRole` instead of substring `toHaveTextContent`.

4. **🔴 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF but UNIFORM-worthy pattern** — `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s three colour resolvers (lines 13-29) are NOT exported, unlike the codebase's own established precedent for exactly this situation: `zimmTextInput.css.ts`'s equivalent resolvers ARE exported and covered by a dedicated `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` (whose own comment states "a mis-ordered branch renders a plausible-but-wrong border... these assertions moved here"). Because `index.test.tsx` globally mocks `useMultiStyleConfig`, `baseStyle` (and therefore these resolvers) is NEVER invoked by any shipped test. Tester proved this is a real blind spot by inverting the disabled/selected precedence in `resolveTextColour` (disabled+selected chip would wrongly get the selected/inverse text colour instead of muted/disabled) — ran the component's own tests, recipeGuards, recipeParts, tsc, eslint, AND the full 722-test suite: 100% green throughout, meaning a real rendering defect would ship silently. Fix: export the three resolvers + add a `.css.test.ts` mirroring `zimmTextInput`'s pattern.

5. **🟡 CONFIRMED, gap in coverage only, code itself correct** — no shipped test calls `rerender()`; Tester wrote and ran a throwaway probe (selectedValue changing post-mount; a value becoming disabled post-mount) — both passed, code is correct, but the re-sync `useEffect` (index.tsx:74-76) has zero coverage in the delivered suite.

6. **🔵 note, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** — `'data-size-value'` string literal repeated 3× with no shared constant (JSX prop + 2 read sites). Mirrors zimmColourSwatchGroup's own unflagged `data-swatch-value` precedent, just split across two files instead of one. Low drift risk (DOM wire-protocol between a component and its own direct parent). Not escalated.

Both required falsifications (disabled-skip in arrow nav, roving-tabindex-updates-on-arrow-nav) were performed as actual break-rerun-revert cycles with real failing output observed both times, then confirmed clean on revert.

## Your job

Score all six axes. In particular weigh:
- Finding #1 (wrong token category, zero-visual-diff fix) — same class of issue Step 1 had, already fixed there. Is a second occurrence in Step 2 acceptable to report-and-move-on, or does recurrence itself argue for fixing now so it doesn't become a 3rd/4th occurrence in Steps 4-6 which reuse this exact recipe pattern?
- Finding #2 (missing i18n extraction) — is running the extraction script and committing the resulting translation file changes IN SCOPE for this component step (the files are Tier 2, Integration/SI-Partner owned per protectedFiles.md's Translations section — is touching them without that owner's involvement appropriate even via the standard extraction tool, or should this be deferred/batched to a later point, e.g. Step 7's final gate, or reported to Marcel as a process gap instead of fixed inline)?
- Finding #3 (tautological test) — this is a real, confirmed test-quality defect fully within this step's own new test file. Cheap to fix (change one assertion).
- Finding #4 (untested colour-precedence logic, real proven blind spot) — real defect risk, established codebase pattern already exists to close it (zimmTextInput precedent), but requires adding a new file (a .css.test.ts) not originally in the step's manifest — is that acceptable scope for a REWORK instruction, or should it be deferred/reported instead since it's more than a single-line fix?

Give PASS or REWORK. If REWORK, give the Implementer a SPECIFIC, bounded instruction — name exactly which findings to fix in this round and which to defer/report to Marcel, and be explicit about whether creating a new zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts file (mirroring zimmTextInput.css.test.ts) is authorized as part of this round's scope or not.

I independently reproduced the Tester's two 🔴 findings via live mutate→test→revert cycles (not just read their report), ran the actual i18n extraction script myself to see the real diff shape, and verified the token-identity claim against `colour.ts` directly. Full detail below.

| **Completeness** | **FAIL** | `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s colour-precedence logic (disabled/selected/default) is untested — I proved this myself by inverting `resolveTextColour`'s branch order and re-running the **entire 722-test suite**: 100% green, tsc clean, eslint clean. testing.md requires coverage for exactly this shape of logic ("pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken"), and an in-repo precedent for closing this exact gap already exists (`zimmTextInput.css.test.ts`). |
| **Conformance** | **FAIL** | `zimmSizeChip.css.ts:15,21` uses a `text.*`-category token (`--zimm-color-text-default`) on `borderColor`/`background`. Confirmed via `colour.ts` that `text.default`, `border.focus`, and `background['05']` are all the literal primitive `grey[900]`/`#191919` — so correct-category tokens exist at the identical value. Zero-visual-diff fix. This is the second occurrence of this exact shape in this build (Step 1's `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts` had it, and it's already been fixed there — confirmed by reading its current code, which correctly uses `--zimm-color-bg-05`). |

The recipe's own comment (`zimmSizeChip.css.ts:40-46`) self-flags the colour pairing as "this file's own best-effort reading... not a pixel-confirmed Figma export" — an honest disclosure, not a false pass, but per this review's own framework that makes the axis UNVERIFIED rather than PASS. |

### What I tried to falsify

1. **Tautological test (finding #3).** Backed up `zimmSizeChipGroup/index.tsx`, mutated `firstEnabledIndex` to unconditionally `return 0`, ran the roving-tabindex tests. Result: `falls back to the first ENABLED size when the first size is disabled` **passed anyway** (`'XS'.includes('S')` under `toHaveTextContent`'s default substring match), while the sibling test `a disabled chip is never the roving tab stop...` correctly **failed** under the identical mutation. Ran tsc, eslint, and the **entire suite** (not just this component's): 722/722 tests, 48/48 files, 100% green. Reverted, confirmed byte-identical, re-ran full suite (722/722 green again). **CONFIRMED** — a real regression here ships completely undetected.
3. **The i18n scope question (finding #2).** Rather than accept "just run extraction and commit" at face value, I ran `npm run extract-default-translations` myself and diffed the result before reverting. It does **not** produce a clean, single-key diff: alongside the wanted `size_chips.group.label`, it also surfaces the still-missing `slide_indicator.position.label` (Step 1's unresolved gap), pulls in ~7 unrelated `product_detail.drawer*`/`details_and_care` keys apparently left over from the just-merged PDP-drawer-tabs PR (#67) never running extraction, and **removes** existing `header.button.assistive_msg.*` keys from `en-US.json`/`en-GB.json`.
